# Load and Clean the Data

This section focuses on loading and performing an initial cleaning of the data. 
I limit the processing here to data cleaning which can be utilized by all the 
following sections. Final data cleaning will occur within their respective
analysis sections.

```{r LAC Setup, include=FALSE}
#| echo: false
library('tidyverse')
library('naniar')
```

## Load & Process Data Frame

Load the final data set received from the Qualtrics survey. I let readr try to
guess the column types, disable the output from that guessing, and set blanks,
'NA', and 'N/A' values to the internal R value of NA.

```{r LAC Load Data}
file_path <- "data_final.csv"                   # Final Data File

# Read in the full CSV into a dataframe.
full_df <- read_csv(file_path,                  # File Path
                    col_types = NULL,           # Type Guessing Column Types
                    show_col_types = FALSE,     # Suppress Output of Col Types
                    na = c("", "NA", "N/A")     # Set these values to NA
)
```

## Initial Data Frame Processing

A character vector is created to hold the columns I will not be using in this
analysis. I then create a new data frame called 'main_df' with the following
modifications made:

- Removing the top 2 header rows
- Removing unwanted/unnecessary columns
- Rename a column that has potentiall problematic characters:
'Duration (in seconds)' to 'Duration'
- Update the columns Finished, Progress, and Duration to their respected data 
types
- Add an index value and make it the first column in the data frame

```{r LAC Clean Dataframe}
columns_to_remove <- c("Q_RelevantIDDuplicate",
                       "Q_RelevantIDDuplicateScore",
                       "Q_RelevantIDFraudScore",
                       "Q_RelevantIDLastStartDate",
                       "ResponseId",
                       "UserLanguage")

# Create a data frame with only the data we want to process
main_df <- full_df |> 
  slice(3:n()) |>                                 # 3rd Observation Onward
  select(-any_of(columns_to_remove)) |>           # Remove Unwanted Variables
  rename(Duration = `Duration (in seconds)`) |>   # Rename Variable
  mutate(
    ID = 1:n(),                                   # Index Value Auto-Increment
    Finished = as.logical(Finished),              # Set to Boolean
    Progress = as.numeric(Progress),              # Set to Numeric
    Duration = as.numeric(Duration)               # Set to Numeric
  ) |>                                          
  relocate(ID)                                    # Make Index First
```

## Understand Current Observation Counts

I will want to understand how the number of observations changes while I clean
the data frame. I will keep two variables and update and report on them for 
every step of the cleaning process. I initialize the variables 'old_count' and 
'new_count' with the current number of records.

```{r LAC Participant Counts}
old_count <- nrow(main_df)
new_count <- nrow(main_df)
```

- Current Observations: `r new_count`

This represents the number of survey participants before any cleaning has been
completed.

## Remove Underage Participants

Due to complexities and legalities when working with individuals under 18 years
of age, I am going to remove them. 

```{r LAC Remove Underage}
main_df |>
  filter(Age == 'Under 18') |>
  nrow()
```
We have no survey participants who self-reported as Under 18.

- Removed Observations: `r old_count - new_count`
- New Observation Count: `r new_count`

## Remove Duplicates

I remove any duplicates that Qualtrics has flagged as a duplicate response. I 
also remove the column from the data frame after this process is completed.

```{r LAC Remove Duplicates}
main_df <- main_df |>
  filter(is.na(Q_DuplicateRespondent)) |>
  select(-Q_DuplicateRespondent)

old_count <- new_count
new_count <- nrow(main_df)
```

- Removed Observations: `r old_count - new_count`
- New Observation Count: `r new_count`

## Remove Significant NAs

Each of the four survey sections (Age_Perception, Ageism_Employment,
Fraboni_Scale, Personal_Experience) is scored and cleaned independently using 
methods appropiate for the data in their sections. Survey takers who enter data 
in a single section is potentially meaningful, and a respondent should not be 
disqualified from the overall results because they skipped other sections.

For that reason, at this stage I only remove respondents who provided no
usable data across any of the four sections. These represent participants who
essentially abandoned the survey immediately after the demographic questions
and have nothing for any downstream section to analyze.

```{r LAC Remove Major NAs}
survey_question_prefixes <- c("Age_Perception", 
                              "Ageism_Employment",
                              "Fraboni_Scale", 
                              "Personal_Experience")

# Per-section NA proportion for every respondent (one column per section) 
section_na_pct <- map(
  survey_question_prefixes, function(p) {
    main_df |>
      select(starts_with(p)) |>
      is.na() |>
      rowMeans()
    }
  ) |>
  set_names(survey_question_prefixes) |>
  as_tibble()

# Keep respondents unless they are 100% missing in every single section
main_df <- main_df |>
  filter(rowSums(section_na_pct == 1) < length(survey_question_prefixes))

old_count <- new_count
new_count <- nrow(main_df)
```

- Removed Observations: `r old_count - new_count`
- New Observation Count: `r new_count`

## Remove Speed-Through & Abandoned

Participants who completed the survey in under 3 minutes likely represent 
click-through respondents where the quality of the received data are likely very 
poor. Responses exceeding 4 hours suggest the survey was abandoned. Both are 
removed from the data frame due to potential low-quality responses.

```{r LAC Remove Time Based Constraints}
main_df <- main_df |>
  filter(Duration >= 180, Duration <= 14400)

old_count <- new_count
new_count <- nrow(main_df)
```

- Removed Observations: `r old_count - new_count`
- New Observation Count: `r new_count`


## Examine no response for Age

I want to look for any participants who did not specify an age after all the
previous cleaning was performed. 

```{r LAC Check for NA for Age}
main_df |>
  filter(is.na(Age)) |>
  nrow()
```

Since no further participants remain that did not specify an age, the data frame
at this time contains participants who provided an age.

## Update The Date Format

Update all date variables to the R standard format using the lubridate package 
with the timezone set to America/Chicago which is the timezone set in my 
Qualtrics profile.

```{r LAC Update Date Format}
main_df <- main_df |>
  mutate(across(c(StartDate, EndDate, RecordedDate), 
                ~ ymd_hms(.x, tz = "America/Chicago")))
```

## Factor The Character Columns

Most character columns are categorical and can take advantage of being factored.
I create a character vector with the variables I plan to factor. I then perform
the factoring of the variables.

```{r LAC CV Variables To Factor}
vars_to_factor <- c("Age",
                    "Gender",
                    "Country",
                    "Education",
                    "IT_Field",
                    "IT_Industry",
                    "Status")

main_df <- main_df |>
  mutate(across(all_of(vars_to_factor), as.factor))
```

## Set Ordered Levels For Ordinal Factors

Unlike the previous factored variables, the variables Age and Education are 
ordinal variables — their categories have a meaningful low-to-high order. 
Setting them as ordered factors here ensures all downstream analyses and graphs 
sort and interpret them correctly without additional recoding. This will be 
especially important in the Spearman correlations later.

```{r LAC Set Ordinals}
main_df <- main_df |>
  mutate(
    Age = factor(Age,
      levels = c(
        "18-24 years old",
        "25-34 years old",
        "35-44 years old",
        "45-54 years old",
        "55-64 years old",
        "65+ years old"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    ),
    Education = factor(Education,
      levels = c(
        "Some high school or no formal schooling",
        "High school diploma, GED or equivalent",
        "Some college, but no degree",
        "Associates, vocational, technical degree or equivalent",
        "Bachelor's degree or equivalent",
        "Graduate degree (MA, MS, MBA, etc.)",
        "Terminal degree (PhD, EdD, JD, MD, DDS, etc.)"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
```

## Inspect The data frame

At this point, I display a summary of the data frame I have performed the
initial cleaning on to see if there are any issues that should be addressed.

```{r LAC Print Summary}
summary(main_df)
```

## Save out the Data Frame

The data frame has been cleaned to a point where the data are usable in future 
analysis. I save out the data frame in RDS format for input into each of the 
different sections of this analysis so they can be independently processed.

```{r LAC Save DataFrame}
saveRDS(main_df, "main_df.rds")
```

## Conclusion
Data from Qualtrics were loaded and an initial cleaning was performed. At this
point not all NA values have been addressed as they will be looked at and
addressed appropriately in their respective sections.

### Cleaning Performed:

- Removed CSV headers
- Removed unwanted and unnecessary columns
- Updated column names to address problematic characters
- Updated the columns Finished, Progress, and Duration to their data types
- Added an index and made it the first column in the data frame
- Removed ineligible participants (under 18 and unidentified)
- Removed duplicates identified by Qualtrics
- Removed observations with excessive NAs
- Removed outlier timed submissions
- Standardized all date formats
- Factored character columns
- Set ordered levels for ordinal factors

### Final Response Counts:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Original responses | 166 |
| Removed during initial cleaning | `r 166 - nrow(main_df)` |
| Final analytic sample | `r nrow(main_df)` |
